about_blocks.text: About Homestead for Hope in Gainsborough, Saskatchewan
about_blocks.html: About Homestead for Hope in Gainsborough, Saskatchewan

about_blocks.text: Homestead for Hope is a residential recovery program for women 18 and over, run by Choose Life Ministry, a Christian non-profit based in Carnduff, Saskatchewan. The program is openly faith-based. Women come for help with addiction, trauma, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm or an unexpected pregnancy, and they live on site for 13 weeks.
about_blocks.html: Homestead for Hope is a residential recovery program for women 18 and over, run by Choose Life Ministry, a Christian non-profit based in Carnduff, Saskatchewan. The program is openly faith-based. Women come for help with addiction, trauma, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm or an unexpected pregnancy, and they live on site for 13 weeks.

about_blocks.text: The house is an original stone farmhouse on 160 acres near Gainsborough, in the far southeast of the province. The ministry renovated it fully. It holds six residents and two live-in staff, with a living room, a dining room that doubles as a library, a shared kitchen, three resident bedrooms with bunk beds and two bathrooms. Outside there is a long gravel lane, open lawn, mature trees, a small stream and a garden plot that residents work.
about_blocks.html: The house is an original stone farmhouse on 160 acres near Gainsborough, in the far southeast of the province. The ministry renovated it fully. about_blocks.text: The 13-week Freedom Program is built around Freedom Session, a Christian discipleship and recovery course. Alongside it, residents get professional counselling, faith-based teaching and worship, and practical life skills. They cook meals together and share the daily running of the house.

about_blocks.text: There is no charge for the program. A $50 application fee holds your place once you are accepted, and food, lodging and program materials are included. Choose Life Ministry relies on donations, including a Second Chance store and non-cash gifts.

about_blocks.text: Programming Director Kassie Holbrook is a licensed practical nurse with about ten years of nursing experience, and she oversees intake and medical needs. Counselling is provided by Kerri Keith and Florence Fullerton, who both hold master's degrees in marriage and family therapy. Intakes run on fixed dates, three times a year in 2027.

about_blocks.text: Gainsborough is a small village close to the Manitoba border. From Regina the drive takes about 3 hours 15 minutes, and Estevan is about an hour away. The ministry office is in Carnduff, around 20 minutes from the farm, and is open Monday to Thursday from 9am to 4pm. Women apply through a form on the website, and a family member or friend can use the same form to nominate someone. The centre does not list detox or outpatient services, so anyone who needs medical withdrawal care should arrange it before the intake date.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Homestead for Hope

faqs.question: What kind of program is Homestead for Hope?

answer_blocks.text: Homestead for Hope is a Christian, faith-based residential program for women 18 and over. Residents live in a restored stone farmhouse near Gainsborough, Saskatchewan for a 13-week Freedom Program that combines professional counselling, faith-based teaching, life skills and community living. It is the residential facility of Choose Life Ministry, a Christian non-profit.

faqs.question: How much does Homestead for Hope cost?

answer_blocks.text: The program is free. Choose Life Ministry charges a $50 application fee once you are accepted, which secures your place. Food, lodging and program materials are all included, and the ministry is funded by donations.
answer_blocks.html: The program is free. Choose Life Ministry charges a $50 application fee once you are accepted, which secures your place. Food, lodging and program materials are all included, and the ministry is funded by donations.

answer_blocks.text: The Freedom Program runs for 13 weeks and starts on set intake dates. For 2027 the centre lists intakes from January 4 to April 10, May 16 to August 14, and September 12 to December 11. Check the intake dates page on the centre's website for the current schedule.

faqs.question: Who can attend Homestead for Hope?

answer_blocks.text: The program is for women aged 18 and older. The centre works with women facing substance use, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm, trauma and abuse, and unexpected pregnancy. The application asks about your faith background, and applicants agree that Christian faith guides the program.

faqs.question: Does Homestead for Hope offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not describe a detox or medical withdrawal service on its website, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. If you are still using alcohol or drugs, ask the team how to arrange withdrawal care before your intake date.

answer_blocks.text: Freedom Session is the Christian discipleship and recovery curriculum at the centre of the program. Homestead for Hope describes it as a way to work on the roots of life-controlling issues through Scripture, community and honest self-reflection. Residents go through it with trained leaders and the other women in the house.

answer_blocks.text: The house has six resident beds in three bedrooms, plus two beds for live-in staff. With so few residents, groups stay small and staff know each woman well.
